9: 
10: = Params
11: 
12: While the query is specified as a plain string, it is usually interpreted as a set of key-value pairs commonly referred to as
13: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Query_string[__URL Parameters__,window=blank_], although here we use the term __query parameters__ or __params__
14: for short.
15: There is no official, standard specification of the query parameters format, but the W3C recommendations and HTML 5 have this to say:
16: 
17: * The query string is composed of a series of key-value pairs.
18: 
19: * Within each pair, the field name and value are separated by an equals sign, "=".
20: 
21: * The series of pairs is separated by the ampersand, "&".
22: 
23: * Most web frameworks allow multiple values to have the same key.
24: 
25: * Key comparisons are usually case-sensitive, but the receiving authority is ultimately responsible for deciding this.
26: 
27: This URL has two query parameters, cpp:first[] and cpp:last[] whose values are "John" and "Doe" respectively:
28: 
29: [source]
30: ----
31: https://www.example.com?first=John&last=Doe
32: ----
33: 
34: [cols="2,3"]
35: |===
36: // Headers
37: |s| `params( s )`
38: 
39: // Row 1, Column 1
40: |`"?first=John&last=Doe"`
41: // Row 1, Column 2
42: |`{ { "first", "John" }, { "last", "Doe" } }`
43: |===
44: 
45: Like the path, the library permits access to the params as using these separate, bidirectional view types which reference the underlying URL:
46: 
47: [cols="1,1,3"]
48: |===
49: // Headers
50: |Type|Accessor|Description
51: 
52: // Row 1, Column 1
53: |cpp:params_view[]
54: // Row 1, Column 2
55: |cpp:url_view_base::params[params]
56: // Row 1, Column 3
57: |A read-only range of decoded params.
58: 
59: // Row 2, Column 1
60: |cpp:params_ref[]
61: // Row 2, Column 2
62: |cpp:url_view_base::params[params]
63: // Row 2, Column 3
64: |A modifiable range of decoded params.
65: 
66: // Row 3, Column 1
67: |cpp:params_encoded_view[]
68: // Row 3, Column 2
69: |cpp:url_view_base::encoded_params[encoded_params]
70: // Row 3, Column 3
71: |A read-only range of params.
72: 
73: // Row 4, Column 1
74: |cpp:params_encoded_ref[]
75: // Row 4, Column 2
76: |cpp:url_view_base::encoded_params[encoded_params]
77: // Row 4, Column 3
78: |A modifiable range of params.
79: 
80: |===
81: 
82: A param always has a key, even if it is the empty string.
83: The value is optional; an empty string is distinct from no value.
84: The lack of an `=` character in the query param is interpreted as no value, while an `=` character with no value is interpreted as an empty string.
85: 
86: [cols="2,3"]
87: |===
88: // Headers
89: |s| `params( s )`
90: 
91: |`"?name=John"`
92: |`{ { "name", "John" } }`
93: 
94: |`"?=John"`
95: |`{ { "", "John" } }`
96: 
97: |`"?name="`
98: |`{ { "name", "" } }`
99: 
100: |`"?name"`
101: |`{ { "name", no_value } }`
102: 
103: |`"?"`
104: |`{ { "", no_value } }`
105: 
106: |`""`
107: |`{}`
108: 
109: |===
110: 
111: To represent individual params the library uses these types, distinguished by their ownership model and whether percent-escapes are possible:
112: 
113: [cols="1,1,3"]
114: |===
115: // Headers
116: |Type|String Type|Description
117: 
118: // Row 1, Column 1
119: |cpp:param[]
120: // Row 1, Column 2
121: |cpp:std::string[]
122: // Row 1, Column 3
123: |A key-value pair with ownership of the strings.
124: This can be used to hold decoded strings, or to
125: allow the caller to take ownership of a param
126: by making a copy.
127: 
128: // Row 2, Column 1
129: |cpp:param_view[]
130: // Row 2, Column 2
131: |cpp:string_view[]
132: // Row 2, Column 3
133: |A key-value pair without percent-escapes,
134: referencing externally managed character buffers.
135: 
136: // Row 3, Column 1
137: |cpp:param_pct_view[]
138: // Row 3, Column 2
139: |cpp:pct_string_view[]
140: // Row 3, Column 3
141: |A key-value pair which may contain percent-escapes,
142: referencing externally managed character buffers.
143: 
144: |===
145: 
146: Param types can be constructed from initializer lists, allowing for convenient notation.
147: To represent a missing value, the constant
148: cpp:no_value[]
149: or cpp:nullptr[] may be used.
150: This table shows some examples of initializer lists used to construct a param type, and the resulting data members:
151: 
152: [cols="2,1,1,1"]
153: |===
154: // Headers
155: |Statement|cpp:qp.key[]|cpp:qp.value[]|cpp:qp.has_value[]
156: 
157: // Row 1, Column 1
158: |`param qp = { "first", "John" };`
159: // Row 1, Column 2
160: |`"First"`
161: // Row 1, Column 3
162: |`"John"`
163: // Row 1, Column 4
164: |cpp:true[]
165: 
166: // Row 2, Column 1
167: |`param qp = { "first", "" };`
168: // Row 2, Column 2
169: |`"First"`
170: // Row 2, Column 3
171: |`""`
172: // Row 2, Column 4
173: |cpp:true[]
174: 
175: // Row 3, Column 1
176: |`param qp = { "first", no_value };`
177: // Row 3, Column 2
178: |`"First"`
179: // Row 3, Column 3
180: |`""`
181: // Row 3, Column 4
182: |cpp:false[]
183: 
184: // Row 4, Column 1
185: |`param qp = { "", "Doe" };`
186: // Row 4, Column 2
187: |`""`
188: // Row 4, Column 3
189: |`"Doe"`
190: // Row 4, Column 4
191: |cpp:true[]
192: 
193: |===
194:

203: This demonstrates how the syntax of the query maps to the parameter structure:
